items.title: Bob Rosengarden interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 6, 1996
items.q: And Igor Stravinsky had signed to do it and he wrote this piece for Benny, and they needed people who could read music because they didn’t want to waste time, and Stravinsky’s writing was difficult.

ctx.x: Well how did the thing with Igor Stravinsky happen. He wrote a piece?

Well I did a lot of work at Columbia Recording Studio. And Igor Stravinsky had signed to do it and he wrote this piece for Benny, and they needed people who could read music because they didn’t want to waste time, and Stravinsky’s writing was difficult. It was one of the very few times, if not the only time, that I ever saw Benny uncomfortable. Where he was not in charge. He was second banana. And I mean Doc Severinsen was in that band. We sat there in that band and just relished it. Like your turn in the barrel,…
He did something for Woody Herman too I think.
